churn_resistance.rationale: Upgrades would touch few files: framework usage is idiomatic, all data access is funneled through two modules, and the undocumented-internal reliance is quarantined in one file. The duplicated API resource types and the absence of any type-checking setup are the main residual churn risks.

findings.issue: The global stylesheet href is computed as `new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname`. In an SSR context import.meta.url is the module's file:// URL, so the href becomes a filesystem-absolute path (e.g. /home/.../app/src/document.css) that 404s in the browser; Vite's docs explicitly state this pattern "does not work with SSR", and the official Gracile starters instead use a plain root-relative path like `/src/document.css` (which Vite's build-html pass rewrites to the hashed asset).
findings.suggestion: Use the documented Gracile idiom: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/document.css" />`, exactly as in the starter projects and the defining-base-document docs, so dev serving and the production asset pipeline both resolve it.

findings.issue: isBuildRender gates data loading on `url.hostname === 'gracile-static'`, which is an undocumented internal stub origin of @gracile/engine's build render pass (dist/routes/render.js: `new URL(pathname, 'http://gracile-static')`), not a public API. If the framework changes that sentinel, the build would either crash or silently start fetching API data at build time, violating the spec's no-build-time-fetch requirement.
findings.suggestion: Keep the single choke point but make it defensive: fail loudly (or also skip) when the handler runs in a non-request context that isn't the known stub host, and watch upstream for a documented build/prerender-detection API; consider a graceful-degradation flag in vite.config instead.

findings.issue: Sprite uses an inline `onerror` attribute to hide broken images — inline JS blocks a future strict CSP and bypasses the app's otherwise framework-managed progressive enhancement.
findings.suggestion: Hide missing sprites with CSS (e.g. a wrapper revealed by default with `img[src]` styling) or handle it from the existing client elements (pokemon-filters / a tiny shared script) instead of an inline handler.

findings.issue: There is no tsconfig.json, no typescript devDependency and no `check` script, so all the route/handler type annotations (and the documented defineRoute ordering constraint that makes props type-check) are never actually verified by anything — Vite only strips them.
findings.suggestion: Add the starter project's tsconfig (extending @gracile/gracile/tsconfigs) plus a `tsc --noEmit` check script, mirroring `npm create gracile@latest -t minimal-server-hono`.

findings.issue: The Move (and related) PokeAPI resource types are defined per-route and duplicated between pokemon/[name].ts and moves/[name].ts; the two copies can drift when the API surface grows.
findings.suggestion: Move the API resource shapes (Species, Pokemon, Move, TypeDetail) into app/src/lib/data.ts alongside the other API types so there is a single typed model of the API.

summary: This app is built squarely on Gracile 0.11's current APIs — the handler/props route shape, server-html documents, the official Hono adapter — with all five dependencies at latest stable majors and nothing the platform doesn't already cover. Data access, URL construction and the one framework-internal workaround are each quarantined in a single module, so framework or requirement changes would touch few files. The notable exceptions are a stylesheet link built with the `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` idiom that Vite documents as non-functional under SSR (likely a production 404) and dependence on the undocumented 'gracile-static' build-render sentinel.
